findings.claim: (4) admin_member_record's parent is the `database` entity (parentCard '1', required), the SAME attachment point as `member` -- NOT parented to person. It carries its own `person` reference property (domain-sharing, required) rather than being a `_parent` child of person (unlike `profile`). Instance `_sharing` is asserted explicitly `domain` at create time. Given this, the bulk-fetch-all-records-for-a-collective query the task proposes, `entity?_type.string=admin_member_record&_parent.reference=<dbEntityId>&props=person,name`, is WIRE-VALID against the schema (database is the correct _parent to filter on) and against the general query-reference doc's `_parent.reference=PARENT_ID` pattern (children of a parent).
findings.evidence: scripts/migrations/lib/mvox-schema-extensions.ts:211-286 (admin_member_record def: parents:[{entity:'database', parentCard:'1', required:true}], properties: person(domain,ref,ordinal1), name(domain,string,ordinal2), phone/email/birthdate(private)). entu-www/src/api/query-reference/index.md:100-102 (`?_parent.reference=PARENT_ID` = children of a parent).

findings.claim: (4) HOWEVER, the codebase's two closest sibling BULK queries (the ones the task names) do NOT filter by `_parent.reference` at all -- both fetch domain-wide with only a type filter + props + limit, relying on Gate-A visibility plus the documented single-collective-per-db invariant, then associate rows to a collective client-side (or not at all): listActiveMembers (rosterData.ts:98-104) is `entity?_type.string=member&status.string=active&props=person,_parent&limit=500` (no parent filter -- doc at lines 74-80 explicitly says 'drops person.reference' and relies on Gate-A admitting every domain-shared member). listSections (sectionData.ts:106) is `entity?_type.string=section&props=name,display_order,_parent&limit=500` (no parent filter either; the #124/F3 comments at +page.svelte:206-236 discuss the resulting multi-org ambiguity this causes and how the page resolves 'whose collective is this' post-hoc from the viewer's OWN row rather than server-side filtering). So there are two live sibling shapes to choose between for admin_member_record, not one: filter server-side by `_parent.reference=<dbEntityId>` (schema-valid, narrower, avoids the #124 ambiguity class outright) OR fetch domain-wide with `props=person,name` only and match client-side by personId (matches the two EXISTING sibling bulk reads' actual shape). This is a genuine open choice, not resolved by precedent alone since the two named siblings disagree with the task's suggested filtered shape.
findings.evidence: src/lib/roster/rosterData.ts:74-80,98-104 (listActiveMembers, no _parent filter). src/lib/sections/sectionData.ts:106 (listSections, no _parent filter). src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:206-236 (#124/F3 ambiguity discussion + client-side dbEntityId resolution from viewer's own row).

findings.claim: (4, critical reasoning) What a domain-tier (member) caller receives for admin_member_record regardless of props=: cleanupEntity (entu-api/utils/entity.js:569-586) selects EXACTLY ONE precomputed bucket per response -- `entity.private` only if the caller is directly in the entity's `access` list (explicit owner/editor/viewer/expander grant), else `entity.domain` if authenticated and the entity is domain-shared, else `entity.public`, else nothing. Because admin_member_record's phone/email/birthdate prop-defs are declared `sharing:'private'` (mvox-schema-extensions.ts:246-271), their VALUES are only ever written into the entity's `private` bucket at write time -- they structurally never exist under `domain` or `public` bucket keys for cleanupEntity to spread out, for ANY caller lacking explicit access. So an ordinary member (domain-tier reader, not owner/editor of the record) gets NO private fields in her response even with a maximally greedy `props=person,name,phone,email,birthdate` request -- the platform partition alone protects her, independent of props=. BUT admin_member_record has `inheritsRights:true` from its `database` parent (mvox-schema-extensions.ts:218), and the collective's admin/owner/editor rights already cascade onto every member/admin_member_record under it (same rights-cascade pattern documented for `member` itself) -- so an ADMIN viewing the roster IS in the entity's `access` list via inheritance, and cleanupEntity would hand HER client the `private` bucket, which DOES contain phone/email/birthdate as written. For the admin's own request, props= narrowing (confirmed above to genuinely restrict the query-level projection) is therefore the ONLY thing standing between her roster-page network response and a payload containing every colleague's private phone/email/birthdate -- the platform partition does not help her case at all, since she legitimately holds private-bucket access. The acceptance's literal wording ('a non-admin's request returns no phone/email/birthdate') describes a case that is ALREADY guaranteed for free by cleanupEntity's bucket selection; the load-bearing case props= narrowing actually defends is the ADMIN's own request, which the acceptance wording doesn't name explicitly but the surrounding contract text ('phone/email/birthdate ... MUST NOT BE FETCHED -- request only what renders') is clearly aimed at.
findings.evidence: /home/ai-teams/projects/entu-api/utils/entity.js:569-586 (cleanupEntity bucket-selection logic). scripts/migrations/lib/mvox-schema-extensions.ts:214-217 (type-level sharing:'domain'/gate 2 comment), 246-271 (private-sharing prop-defs), 218 (inheritsRights:true), 219-223 (parent = database, same attachment as member, 'reuses the existing collective owner/editor=admin rights cascade').
